_README: Hand-written ARPAbet for headwords no reference source covers.
These exist because ElevenLabs demonstrably mis-reads them. Each was
synthesised without a dictionary and transcribed back; what came out was
a different word, not a near miss - 'annealed' as 'I kneeled', 'amide' as
'A me day', 'adze' as 'Odd Zai'. See tools/pronunciation/deferred_survey.csv.
Unlike everything else in the pipeline these are NOT generated. A human
wrote them, so a human is the authority for them. They still go through
`validate` - the length gate and the recognition gate both apply - but a
recognition failure on a rare word is expected and does not by itself mean
high   - standard English or well-established technical term
medium - loanword or proper noun where usage genuinely varies; the
reading below is defensible but not the only one. Worth a
This file is version-controlled. tools/pronunciation/ is not.

abs.note: abdominal muscles. CMUdict lists both AE1 B Z and the spelled-out EY1 B IY1 EH1 S (A-B-S); g2p picked the letters. Both readings stress the first vowel, so the stress-ambiguity check cannot separate them - they differ in syllable count, not stress position. Hand-written because the catalogue means the muscles.
